title: Authorize the extension id passed to SecretStorage RPC
body:
`MainThreadSecretState` takes `extensionId` off the wire and uses it directly as the storage namespace for `$getPassword`, `$setPassword`, `$deletePassword` and `$getKeys`. Nothing checks that the extension host on the other end of the connection has anything to do with that extension.

`ExtensionSecrets` does bind the id to the calling extension's own identifier, but it does so on the extension host side — the far side of the connection — so it cannot be what the workbench relies on. A remote extension host runs code from the remote machine, while the store it reaches here is the local secret store, holding the tokens of UI extensions such as the authentication providers. A remote host could therefore name a local extension and read, overwrite or delete its secrets.

The change resolves the extension's running location on the workbench side, which is the trusted answer to where an extension actually runs, and refuses the call when its kind differs from the connection's kind. This follows the same shape as the `extHostContext.extensionHostKind` check already used in `mainThreadAuthentication.ts` and `mainThreadMcp.ts`.

Two details worth a reviewer's attention:

- An extension this window does not run is refused as well, because secrets belonging to a disabled or uninstalled extension can still be sitting in the store, and nothing legitimate asks for a namespace with no running extension behind it.
- Identifiers are compared through `ExtensionIdentifier.toKey`, so case cannot be used to slip past the check.

This separates hosts, not extensions within a host. Extensions sharing a host share a process and can already reach each other's state, so a check at that granularity would not be a boundary; I have left it alone deliberately rather than by oversight.

## Testing

`src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadSecretState.test.ts` adds 11 tests: a remote host naming a local extension is refused for get, set, delete and keys, with the stored secret asserted unchanged in each case; a differently-cased identifier does not get through; the local host naming a remote extension is refused the same way; an extension this window does not run is refused; and each host reaches its own extension normally, including through a differently-cased identifier.

Seven of the eleven fail without the change and all four positive-path tests keep passing, so they are pinning the behaviour rather than restating it.

`tsc -p src` and `eslint` are clean.

title: Fix unresponsive compact menu bar in the Modern UI activity bar
body:
## Description

With `workbench.experimental.modernUI` enabled, the compact (hamburger) menu bar in the activity bar appears unresponsive — clicking it either does nothing visible or renders a sliver of a menu clipped into the icon rail. Disabling the setting was the known workaround.

**Root cause:** `floatingPanels.css` centered the rail's icon column with `transform: translateX(...)` on `.part.activitybar > .content`. A transformed element becomes the containing block for its `position: fixed` descendants, so the compact menu bar's menu (`.menubar-menu-items-holder`, placed by `Menubar.showCustomMenu` in viewport coordinates) was offset by the rail's position and then clipped away by the part's `overflow: hidden`.

### Changes

- **`floatingPanels.css`** — centering is now a `padding-left` with the same computed offset, which no longer establishes a containing block or stacking context. The comment records why this must stay a plain layout offset.

  ```css
  .monaco-workbench.floating-panels .part.activitybar > .content {
  -	transform: translateX(calc((var(--modern-ui-activitybar-lane) - 2px) / 2));
  +	padding-left: calc((var(--modern-ui-activitybar-lane) - 2px) / 2);
  }
  ```

- **`modernUI.contribution.test.ts`** — new test `keeps floating rail overlays anchored to the viewport` builds the compact menu bar DOM inside a floating rail and asserts the fixed menu keeps its viewport coordinates and full width. It fails against the previous CSS (`left: 256, top: 142` instead of `240/120`).

### Notes for review

Rendering is unaffected: `PartLayout.layout` gives `.content` an inline `width`, and `.content` is `content-box`, so the padding grows its border box exactly as the translate shifted it. Comparing both variants in Chromium, `.action-item`, `.action-label`, `.active-item-indicator`, `.badge`, `.menubar` and the hamburger glyph land at identical rects at both densities; only the fixed menu moves. Nothing measures the content area's DOM width — the composite bar's overflow computation uses the `Dimension` passed from `ActivitybarPart.layout`.

title: agentHost: Own SDK auto-download preference

## Summary

- Offer the Agent Host SDK download whenever the SDK is missing, independent of GitHub sign-in, entitlement resolution, or the signed-out experiment.
- Persist each SDK's download-on-use consent in the Agent Host's `agent-host-storage.json`, on the machine that owns the SDK cache.
- Record consent only when the user clicks **Download** or an agent turn actually starts a lazy SDK download; never infer consent from cache presence.

body:
**Environment:**
- VS Code version: 1.136.1 (commit a44adf7f)
- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (build 25F84)
- Arch: arm64

**Relevant settings:**
```json
"workbench.sideBar.location": "right"
```

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Set `"workbench.sideBar.location": "right"`.
2. Reload the window.
3. Switch between side bar views — e.g. open the Explorer, then switch to Search (or vice versa).

**Actual behavior:**
The side bar renders at a very narrow width (well below its previously-set width) each time a view is opened/switched, requiring the sash to be manually dragged wider every time.

**Expected behavior:**
The side bar retains its set/remembered width when switching views, regardless of which edge it's docked to.

**Additional notes / what's been ruled out:**
- Started the same day VS Code auto-updated to 1.136.1 — did not happen on the prior version.
- Reproduces with a clean extension set — ruled out installed extensions as a factor by uninstalling the ones most likely to interact with sidebar/auxiliary-bar layout, with no change.
- Ruled out `workbench.activityBar.location` as a factor — reproduces identically whether it's `"top"` or the default (`"side"`).
- Setting `"workbench.sideBar.location": "left"` (the default) resolves the issue immediately and completely — this appears to be specific to the right-side placement.

title: Report a browser tool failure with an empty message as a failure
body:
Follow-up to #330707. That PR merged with two review points from @dmitrivMS unaddressed. I replied at the time saying both were fixed in it, on the mistaken belief that it had not merged yet. It had, and neither change landed. Nothing has touched `errorResult` since.

## An empty error message reports success to the model

`errorResult` set `toolResultError` to the raw message, unlike the conversion sixteen lines above it, which already falls back:

```ts
...(result.error !== undefined ? { toolResultError: result.error || failedMessage, toolResultMessage: failedMessage } : {}),
```

So `errorResult('')` left `toolResultError` falsy, and that is the sole error signal downstream:

```ts
// agentHostSessionHandler.ts
const isError = !!result.toolResultError;
...
success: !isError,
```

The call was serialized as a success with `error: undefined`, while `toolResultMessage` still set the completed row to "Browser action failed". The user saw a failure, the model was told it succeeded.

Three call sites can produce an empty message, all of the form `e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)`, which is `''` for both `new Error()` and `throw ''`: `playwrightInvoke` in `browserToolHelpers.ts` (used by the click, type, hover, drag, navigate and screenshot tools), the deferred-result wait in `runPlaywrightCodeTool.ts`, and `handleDialogBrowserTool.ts`. The fourth site prefixes its message and was never affected.

The fix falls back to the same label the conversion uses, for the content part as well as the error, so the model is given a reason rather than an empty string.

## The comment on `failedMessage` was wrong

It asserted these tools "declare only an `invocationMessage`". They do not: the screenshot tool prepares "Captured browser screenshot", and `didExecuteTool` keeps a prepared past-tense label unless the result carries a `toolResultMessage`. That is the mechanism @dmitrivMS described, and the comment still stated the version I had wrong. Rewritten to say what the constant is actually for.

## Tests

`errorResult with an empty message still reports a failure` covers both the error signal and the content part. It mirrors the existing empty-message test for `invokeFunctionResultToToolResult`, which had no `errorResult` counterpart. Without the source change it fails on the first assertion; with it the file is 6 passing. No new type errors, 349 before and after.
